project.name: Finn Website Integration
project.primary_goal: Wire Finn into the website as the candidate-facing AI agent and candidate experience layer.

agent.name: Finn
agent.mission: Guide candidates through discovery, engagement, application, interview coordination, follow-up, and status communication while escalating high-value or sensitive interactions to a human recruiter.

steps: Inspect the existing repository and identify the framework, routing, component system, styling approach, authentication, API layer, analytics, and deployment configuration.
Preserve the current Newport visual system and reuse existing components, tokens, typography, spacing, and responsive patterns.
Search the repository for existing Finn assets before creating placeholders.
Implement Finn as a reusable component rather than hard-coding him into one page.
Keep AI/provider credentials server-side and use environment variables. Never expose secrets in browser code.
Use existing backend/API conventions where available. If no agent endpoint exists, create an adapter interface with a safe mock/fallback state so the UI can ship independently.
Run the repository's existing lint, typecheck, tests, and build commands after implementation.
Do not rewrite unrelated website functionality.

entry_points.behavior: Persistent but unobtrusive launcher on desktop and mobile. Opens the Finn experience.
Contextual CTA inviting the candidate to ask about the role, application process, or next steps.

welcome.headline: Meet Finn
welcome.message: I’m Newport’s candidate experience agent. I can help you explore opportunities, understand a role, and navigate next steps.

capabilities.description: Help candidates discover relevant open opportunities.
capabilities.fallback: Direct the candidate to the website's existing jobs/search experience.

capabilities.description: Answer questions using verified job data and approved website/company content.
capabilities.guardrail: Never invent compensation, location, requirements, client identity, interview stages, or hiring status.

capabilities.description: Collect candidate interest and basic information using the site's existing application/intake flow.
capabilities.guardrail: Collect only information required by the existing workflow and privacy policy.

capabilities.description: Escalate to a human recruiter when requested or when Finn cannot safely answer.
triggers: candidate-specific hiring decision or status unavailable to Finn

future_connectors.status: adapter-ready; do not assume API implementation exists

ui_requirements.performance: Lazy-load Finn's conversational UI where practical.
ui_requirements.visual_direction: Use the existing Newport website design system. Finn should feel native to the site, not like a third-party chatbot widget.

requirements: No API keys or provider secrets in client-side bundles.
Sanitize and validate user input at trust boundaries.
Do not expose internal prompts, system configuration, recruiter notes, or private candidate records.
Do not claim access to candidate status unless verified data is actually available.
Respect existing consent, privacy, cookie, and analytics mechanisms.
Log operational errors without unnecessarily logging candidate PII.

files_to_create_or_modify.instruction: Determine exact paths from the repository rather than assuming framework-specific paths.

acceptance_criteria: Finn is available from the intended website entry points on desktop and mobile.
The experience matches the existing Newport brand and design system.
Users can open, close, and interact with Finn without navigation breakage.
Finn receives relevant page/job context when available.
Human recruiter handoff is clearly available.
Loading, empty, offline, API failure, and handoff states are handled gracefully.
Accessibility basics pass for keyboard use, focus, labels, and contrast using the repository's standards.
Analytics events are emitted through the website's existing analytics layer when one exists.
Claude Code returns a concise summary of changed files, architecture decisions, environment variables required, tests run, and any remaining integration dependencies.

deliverables: Tests appropriate to the existing stack
README or implementation notes for configuration
